When a grapnel lands on stone, concrete, or similar hard materials, it rings loudly – it has a Hearing distance of 4 yards (see p. B358). Padding can muffle the noise, reducing this distance to 2 yards. Unpadded: $20, 2 lbs. Padded: $30, 3 lbs.

name: Harpoon
description: A long spike with a hardened tip and an attached rope, this grappling harpoon isn’t the hand-thrown weapon on the Muscle-Powered Ranged Weapon Table, but a projectile for a heavy crossbow or a scorpion. If any damage penetrates the target’s DR, the harpoon lodges there, providing a fixed anchor point for a line. Launched with sufficient force, it may even be driven into stone or concrete (loudly – Hearing distance is 2 yards). Maximum weight supported is 60 lbs. per point of penetrating damage. $30, 2 lbs.

name: Camouflage Paint
description: Paint can be used to camouflage the skin. Suitable colors obtained from crushed leaves, moss, algae, mud, soot, and so on are applied to the face, neck, hands, etc. If all exposed skin is covered and appropriate camouflage clothing is worn, this gives an additional +1 (quality) to Camouflage. $10, neg.

name: Hunting Shirt
description:
This is a baggy, thigh-length overshirt of durable material with straps, cords, or loops for attaching suitable foliage. Fringed sleeves help to break up the silhouette even further; optionally, a blotchy dye job completes the effect.

A plain shirt gives +1 (quality) to Camouflage; a dyed one, +2. This bonus may be improved further through customization, which requires 20 hours and a Camouflage roll. Each point of success adds another +1, to a maximum of +3, for a total of up to +5. The shirt requires specific preparation for terrain, climate, and season – and like regular clothing, if it’s inappropriate for the background, it might give a Camouflage penalty. Plain: $50, 5 lbs. Dyed: $100, 5 lbs.

name: Blanket
description: A moderately heavy cloth, placed over a horse’s back before it’s ridden. This prevents chafing of the rider’s legs and the horse’s sides, and partially cushions the rider’s weight, giving both horse and rider +1 to HT-based rolls to resist FP loss. $25, 2.5 lbs.

name: Bridle
description: Developed in Ukraine around 4000 B.C., the bridle is a band that goes around a horse’s nose, with straps to keep it in place. It provides an attachment point for reins, and can also be used to lead the horse. A bridle gives a Riding bonus that partly offsets the -3 for controlling a horse by leg pressure: +1 if the reins are held one-handed (net -2), or +2 if they’re held two-handed (net -1). $10, 2 lbs.

name: Bridle and Bit
description: A bridle augmented by a mouthpiece – usually made of metal – that fits into a gap between the horse’s teeth. This gives the rider enhanced control: +2 to Riding if the reins are held one-handed (net -1), or +3 if they’re held two-handed (no penalty). $35, 3 lbs.

name: Halter
description: A piece of harness designed for tying up or leading a horse; it gives +1 to Animal Handling for this purpose. It resembles a bridle but provides no Riding bonus. Conversely, a bridle can’t safely be used to tether a horse; a horse struggling to free itself from a bridle can injure itself, suffering thrust-1 crushing damage based on its own ST. Halters are available for many other species of domesticated animals. $5, 1.5 lbs.

name: Riding Crop
description: A length of cane, typically 2’-3’, wrapped in braided leather, with a short length of flexible leather at the end. Used to tap or strike a horse’s sides, it gives +1 to Riding to control the mount. It can be wielded in the same hand that holds the reins. $10, 1 lb.

name: Saddle, Cushioned
description: Developed by the Scythians around 400 B.C., this is a pair of cushions, one for each side of the horse’s back, held together by wooden arches front and back. It distributes the rider’s weight more effectively, giving horse and rider +2 to HT-based rolls to resist FP loss. It also makes the rider’s seat more stable, giving +1 to Riding to stay mounted and halving encumbrance penalties to Riding (drop fractions). With horse blanket: $100, 10 lbs.

name: Saddle, Horned
description: Used by the Celts around 100 B.C. and adopted by the Roman army 300 years later, the horned saddle has a rigid frame with vertical protrusions at the four corners. These improve the bracing of the rider’s thighs, giving +3 to Riding to stay mounted; even an unconscious rider remains mounted on 10 or less on 3d. Dismounting quickly is tricky: -2 to skill rolls to jump off. A horned saddle eliminates encumbrance penalties to Riding, and gives horse and rider +2 to HT-based rolls to resist FP loss. With horse blanket: $200, 20 lbs.

name: Saddle, Riding
description: Used by the Thracians around 300 B.C., the standard riding saddle has a rigid frame that provides a more stable seat than a cushioned saddle, with a low pommel in front and a low cantle in back. It grants +2 to Riding to remain mounted, eliminates encumbrance penalties to Riding, and gives horse and rider +2 to HT-based rolls to resist FP loss. With horse blanket: $150, 15 lbs.

name: Spurs
description: This Roman invention dates to the first century B.C. In the later Middle Ages, spurs became emblems of nobility, and were often ornate, usually by being gilded or made of silver. Spurs give +1 to Riding to control a horse. $25, neg.

name: Horseshoes
description: Developed around 1000 A.D., horseshoes protect the horse’s feet, especially when it’s carrying heavy loads. They give the horse +2 to HT-based rolls to resist FP loss; as well, they prevent crippling on hard surfaces. Per set: $50, 4 lbs.

name: Saddle, War
description: This saddle has a pommel in front and a high cantle in back for the rider to brace against. It gives all the benefits of a horned saddle (above), but no penalty to dismount. With horse blanket: $250, 30 lbs.

name: Stirrups
description:
Most likely invented in Central Asia, stirrups are shown in Chinese art dated 322 A.D., and reached Western Europe by 700 A.D. They allow vaulting onto a horse with no skill penalty, or climbing on more slowly without a skill roll (see p. B396). They give +1 to Riding to control a mount.

The rider can stand in his stirrups to attack, gaining the benefit of an extra foot of height over his foe. With a war saddle (but not a horned saddle), he can use his leg muscles to press his back into the cantle, creating a firm base for a couched lance; this is standard for Lance skill. $125, 5 lbs.

name: Mats
description: An early design for camel gear: several thick mats piled up in front of the hump, creating a high platform. This is normally used for cargo; riders have -2 to Riding to stay seated. The weight is a major burden. $75, 100 lbs.

name: Bridle and Bit
description: Developed when camels came into use as riding animals, these items resemble similar horse equipment; differences of detail reflect the different mouth structure. Bridle and bit give +2 to Riding to control the mount when used one-handed, or +3 when used two-handed. $35, 3 lbs.

name: Camel Stick
description: Used by riders seated behind the hump to reach forward and tap or strike the camel’s sides, this stick gives +1 to Riding skill to control the mount. $10, 2 lbs.

name: Saddle, Cushion
description: This is purely a riding saddle. It consists of a loop of padding that circles the camel’s hump, held in place by wooden poles at front and back. It grants +1 to Riding to stay mounted. $150, 50 lbs.

name: Saddle, Early Riding
description: Developed in southern Arabia around 1200 B.C., this is the oldest design for a camel saddle. A saddlebow in front of the hump provides support for a cushion behind it. Cargo can be placed on the saddlebow. It gives +1 to Riding to stay mounted. $150, 25 lbs.

name: Saddle, Framed
description: The most familiar sort of camel saddle, this was developed in northern Arabia around 500 B.C. and allowed the use of camels in combat. Saddlebows at the front and back, supported by cushions, are linked by frames along the sides that support a platform on top, where the rider sits, atop the hump. The weight is transmitted to the camel’s ribs rather than resting on the hump. This gives +5 to Riding to stay seated (cancelling the -5 for sitting on the hump). $350, 50 lbs.

name: Saddle, Shoulder
description: This North African camel saddle puts the rider on the camel’s shoulders. A high pommel and cantle give +2 to Riding to stay seated; in addition, the rider can use his toes to help control the camel, for +1 to Riding. $250, 25 lbs.

name: Ankus
description: This goad is used by riders to control elephants. One end has a sharp metal hook used to tug at sensitive points on the elephant’s head or body, especially its ears. It can also be reversed and used to strike the elephant. An ankus gives +1 to Riding or Animal Handling rolls to control an elephant. To use it as a weapon, see its entry in Melee Weapons (p. 54). $45, 1 lb.

name: Logs
description: It’s convenient to figure a log’s statistics from length rather than volume. For a 12”-diameter log, buoyancy is 25 lbs., weight is 25 lbs., and cost is $6 – all per foot of length. For other diameters, multiply these three figures by the square of (diameter/12”); e.g., a 6”-diameter log has a multiplier of 0.25, making buoyancy and weight 6.25 lbs., and cost $1.50, per foot.

name: Improvised Bandages
description:
At TL0, bandages can be made from the cloth manufactured by some Neolithic societies, or from barkcloth (see Paper and Its Cousins, p. 24). Broad, flat leaves are another option, where available; roll against Naturalist as described for finding vines under Tourniquet (p. 145), and note that some leaves have medicinal effects (see Drugs, pp. 150-152).

At TL1-4, bandages can be cut from garments, bedding, etc. Primitive cloth bandages are half-price ($5); leaves and scraps are free. All give -2 to skill and are rarely sterile – roll for infection (p. B444), assuming ordinary “clean” dirt.

name: Dental Forceps
description: Designed to grip a tooth and pull it out. This requires a ST-based Surgery roll; add the +2 for a firm grip. Basic forceps will work, but at -2, canceling out the bonus for a good grip. Critical success gets the entire tooth; ordinary success leaves 1d/2 splinters (round up) that must be extracted separately; ordinary failure leaves the tooth in place; and critical failure inflicts 1d-3 HP of injury to the face. $50, 0.5 lb.

name: Dental Splinter Forceps
description: Used to extract the roots of a broken-off tooth; no additional skill roll required. $50, neg.

name: Scalpel
description: Used to make incisions. $30, neg.

name: Small Kit
description: A typical kit would have forceps, hooks, needles, probes, and scalpels, plus a supply of thread or sinew for stitching up wounds, and material for bandages. Basic equipment for Surgery. $300, 15 lbs.

name: Large Kit
description: A typical kit would include the equivalent of two small kits, with more specialized forms of the basic instruments, plus bone chisels and small hammers – and at TL2, arrow spoons, catheters, cauteries, and specula. Good equipment, giving +1 (quality) to Surgery. $1,500, 40 lbs.

name: Cataract Needles
description: A cataract needle is a very fine, sharp piece of metal, designed to pierce the eyeball with minimal injury. It can push a cataract away from the pupil, sever pieces of it, or press it down to fix it into place. See also Surgical Techniques (p. 12). $50, neg.

name: Eyelash Cautery
description: A fine iron needle with a handle, this is heated and used to burn out the root of an ingrown eyelash after the hair is plucked out. $125, neg.

name: Eyelash Forceps
description: A tiny set of grippers that can seize and pull out an ingrown eyelash (see Forceps, p. 148). $125, neg.

name: Acupuncture Needles
description: Extremely fine needles used in acupuncture, made of bronze at TL1-2 or of steel at TL3+. Per 100: $50, 0.25 lb.

name: Moxa Bundle
description: A cone of dried mugwort leaves for moxibustion. Free, if leaves are gathered in the wild; this requires a Naturalist roll, followed by a Pharmacy (Herbal) or Esoteric Medicine (Moxibustion) roll at +2 to prepare them. A prepared bundle costs $1. Negligible weight.

name: Lancet
description: A specialized knife for opening a vein. Use requires Surgery and Esoteric Medicine rolls. Failure at Surgery causes useless superficial bleeding. Critical failure opens an artery! Handle this using Bleeding (p. B420), with -2 to the required HT rolls. $25, neg.

name: Olive Oil
description: Oil pressed from olives has been used around the Mediterranean since the Neolithic. This is a high-quality oil, and thus expensive, but counts as basic equipment. Treat standard fuel oil (p. B288) as improvised, for -2 (quality) to skill. Per pint: $6, 1 lb.

name: Lanolin
description: A waxy substance extracted from sheep’s wool by washing it in water. It naturally penetrates human skin, giving +1 (quality) to creams and ointments prepared with it. It also gives +1 to HT rolls to regain lost HP after skin injuries. Per pint: $20, 1 lb.

name: Lotion
description: An emulsion prepared from water and some form of fat or oil. Herbal additives provide texture, scent, or therapeutic effects. Basic lotion gives the same benefits as olive oil; good or fine lotion gives +1 or +2 (quality) at +4 or +19 CF. Per pint: $8, 1 lb.

name: Massage Supplies
description: Includes a small brazier, vessels for heating oil and water, a towel that can be warmed and applied dry or wet, and a stock of consumables: oils and lotions to provide lubrication, scents, compounds to stimulate the skin, and fuel (usually charcoal) for heating. $50, 10 lbs. Replacement supplies: $10 after each day of use.

name: Massage Table
description: A table large enough for an adult to lie on at full length, with a smooth surface. It normally has a pillow or a cushion to support the ankles (for someone lying prone) or the knees (for a supine subject). $150, 50 lbs.

name: Massage Chair
description: A chair designed to sit in while being massaged. It provides optimal exposure of the body to the masseur, and can be adjusted to different body sizes and postures. The typical posture has the subject leaning forward with his back exposed. Gives +1 (quality) to skill. $250, 30 lbs.

name: Fine Equipment (+2)
description: At least $10,000 on “basic” items, plus machines that measure striking pressure, a regulation cage or ring, and a full range of the gear on pp. 233-234.

name: Best Equipment (+TL/2, minimum +2)
description: A building-sized setup that costs at least $1 million – be it a secret commando base, state-of-the-art Olympic facility, the Shaolin Temple, or a superhero danger room. Until TL6, the bonus is no higher than the +2 for “fine” equipment, but hundreds of students at once can benefit from it.

name: Shield
description: A large, handheld target for kicking and kneeing. Provides DR 3 vs. crushing (DR 2 vs. other damage). $50, 2 lbs.

name: Heavy Pads
description: Larger mitts for punching and kicking. Give the hands DR 5 vs. crushing (DR 3 vs. other damage) and Bad Grip 3. $75, 5 lbs. (pair).

name: Body Pads
description: Groin and stomach protection that allows kicks and knees to the body. Give the torso DR 4 vs. crushing (DR 2 vs. other damage). $60, 8 lbs.

name: Blanket
description: A warm bedroll. $20, 4 lbs.

name: Canteen
description: Miniature wooden barrel on a strap. Won’t shatter in combat! Holds 1 quart of liquid (2 lbs. if water). $10, 3 lbs.

name: Fishhooks and Line
description: Basic equipment for Fishing skill. Needs a pole. $50, 0.1 lb.

name: Group Basics
description: Basic equipment for Cooking and Survival skill for a group – cook pots, rope, hatchet, etc., for 3-8 campers. $50, 20 lbs.

name: Personal Basics
description: Minimum gear for camping; -2 to Survival rolls without it. Includes utensils, tinderbox, and flint and steel. $5, 1 lb.

name: Pouch or Purse
description: Holds 3 lbs. of small items (coins, personal basics, etc.). $10, 0.2 lb.

name: Rations
description: One meal of dried meat, cheese, etc. $2, 0.5 lb.

name: Sleeping Fur
description: A winter bedroll, suitable for ice caves, arctic adventures, etc. $50, 8 lbs.

name: Sundial, Miniature
description: On a neck chain. Tells time, and allows Navigation at only -1 for equipment – but only in sunlight. $40, 1 lb.

name: Hip Quiver, Large
description: Holds 50 arrows or bolts. Two compartments. $30, 2 lbs.

name: Lanyard, Chain
description: Lets you retrieve dropped weapon on a DX roll. Each attempt requires a Ready maneuver. Can be cut: -6 to hit, DR 4, HP 6. $15, 0.5 lb.

name: Lanyard, Leather
description: As chain lanyard, but only DR 2, HP 2. $1, 0.1 lb.

name: Whetstone
description: For sharpening weapons. $5, 1 lb.

name: Barrel
description: Holds 5 gallons of liquid (40 lbs. if water). DR 1, HP 11. $65, 20 lbs.

name: Bottle
description: Holds 1 quart of liquid (2 lbs. if water). DR 1, HP 4. $3, 1 lb.

name: Bottle, Small
description: Holds 1 pint of liquid (1 lb. if water). DR 1, HP 2. $2, 0.5 lb.

name: Bucket
description: With rope handle. Holds 1 gallon of liquid (8 lbs. if water). DR 1, HP 6. $15, 4 lbs.

name: Chest, Wooden
description: Holds 400 lbs. or 5 cubic feet of loot. Has brackets for two poles; add Basic Lift of carriers to assess encumbrance. DR 2, HP 14. $200, 40 lbs.

name: Sack
description: Holds 40 lbs. of loot. Requires two hands or a pole. DR 1, HP 5. $30, 3 lbs.

name: Strongbox, Iron
description: Holds 40 lbs. of coins or other small items. DR 12, HP 10. $250, 15 lbs.

name: Vial, Crystal
description: Holds half a pint of liquid (0.5 lb. if water). Thick, with stopper – good for collecting corrosive blood, etc. DR 1, HP 1. $5, 0.25 lb.

name: Candle, Beeswax
description: Sufficient to read by. Lasts 24 hrs. $5, 1 lb.

name: Candle, Tallow
description: Smell may attract monsters! Lasts 12 hrs. $0.50, 1 lb.

name: Lantern
description: Eliminates darkness penalties in a two-yard radius. Requires a hand. Burns for 24 hours on 1 pint of oil. $20, 2 lbs.

name: Oil
description: For lanterns. Not useful as a flaming weapon. Per pint: $2, 1 lb.

name: Torch
description: Eliminates darkness penalties in a two-yard radius. Requires a hand. Burns for 1 hr. $3, 1 lb.

name: Bandages
description: Cloth bandages for a half-dozen wounds. Basic equipment for First Aid skill. $10, 1 lb.

name: First Aid Kit
description: Complete kit for treating wounds. +1 to First Aid skill. $50, 2 lbs.

name: Litter
description: For carrying wounded allies (or loot!) weighing up to 200 lbs. Requires two bearers; add their Basic Lift to assess encumbrance. $50, 25 lbs.

name: Surgical Instruments
description: Basic equipment for Surgery skill. Also useful for removing mana organs, eyeballs, etc., from dead monsters without ruining them. $300, 15 lbs.

name: Cord, 3/16”
description: Mainly for pull-ropes and trip-ropes. Supports 90 lbs. Per 10 yards: $1, 0.5 lb.

name: Iron Spike
description: For spiking doors, anchoring traps, etc. $1, 0.5 lb.

name: Ladder, 10’
description: Wooden. For scaling walls and crossing chasms. $25, 15 lbs.

name: Pole, 6’
description: For lifting chests, pitching tents, prodding traps, etc. $5, 3 lbs.

name: Rope, 3/4”
description: Supports 1,100 lbs. Per 10 yards: $25, 5 lbs.

name: Drum
description: Audible for miles! Two-handed. $40, 2 lbs.

name: Harp or Zither
description: Can play softly enough not to be heard through a door. Two-handed. $250, 3 lbs.

name: Horn
description: Audible for miles! Two-handed; speech is impossible. $100, 2 lbs.

name: Stringed
description: Cittern, lute, oud, etc. Two-handed. $150, 5 lbs.

name: Whistle
description: For signaling – not suitable for Bard-Song. $5, 0.1 lb.

name: Woodwind
description: Bamboo flute, tin whistle, or similar. Two-handed; speech is impossible. $40, 1 lb.

name: Balance and Weights
description: Can precisely weigh up to 2 lbs. of gold, magic herbs, etc. $35, 3 lbs.

name: Crowbar, 3’
description: For Forced Entry. Treat as a small mace in combat, at -1 to skill. $20, 3 lbs.

name: File
description: Can saw through hinge, padlock, etc., in (DR + HP) minutes. $40, 1 lb.

name: Hatchet
description: For Forced Entry, cutting firewood, etc. Treat as a hatchet in combat, at -1 to skill. $15, 2 lbs.

name: Mallet
description: For Forced Entry, driving iron spikes, staking vampires, etc. Treat as a small mace in combat, at -1 to skill. $15, 3 lbs.

name: Saw
description: Used to hack off valuable horns, tusks, etc. $150, 3 lbs.

name: Tool Kit, Backpack
description: Basic equipment for one of Armoury, Smith, etc. Other skills can use it, but at -2. $600, 20 lbs.

name: Wheelbarrow
description: Holds 350 lbs. Can be pushed, or harnessed behind someone. Divide effective weight of load by 5. $60, 18 lbs.

name: Paper, 20 Sheets
description: Heavy papyrus or similar, suitable for maps or magical writings. $20, 1 lb.

name: Scribe’s Kit
description: Quills, inkbottles, and penknife. $50, 2 lbs.

name: Anti-Garrote Collar
description: Gives +4 DR vs. strangling and garroting damage (but not neck blows). Can be worn with armor. $35, 1 lb.

name: Delver’s Webbing
description: Belt and suspenders with pouches for 20 lbs. of potions, gadgets, knives, etc. Readying a carried item takes just one Ready maneuver – and is a free action with a suitable Fast-Draw roll. Gives +1 to DX and Fast-Draw rolls to reach these items. Rumored to be the work of brownies! $160, 3 lbs.

name: Helmet Lamp
description: Shuttered, hands-free lantern that throws a five-yard beam. Attaches to all popular helmet patterns. Burns for 12 hours on 1 pint of oil. $100, 2 lbs.

name: Potion Belt
description: Belt with four slots, each of which can carry one “grenade” bottle or two potion vials. Wearer can reach them with Ready or Fast-Draw. Padding removes risk of accidental breakage and gives containers +2 DR vs. deliberate attacks. $60, 1 lb.

name: Quick-Release Backpack
description: Holds 40 lbs. of gear. Dropping it is a free action. Items liable to break if dropped must check for this (1 on 1d if unsure). $300, 3 lbs.

name: Alchemist’s Matches
description: Start fires in just one second! Waterproof tin of 50. May set fire to a pack if dropped (1 on 1d). $15, 0.25 lb.

name: Compass
description: Allows Navigation rolls at no penalty for equipment. $50, 5 lbs.

name: Dwarven Rations
description: One meal of nasty, hard bread. A steady diet (a month or more) gives Resistant to Poison (+3) while continued. $5, 1 lb.

name: Elven Rations
description: Tasty wafers of Essential Food. Three meals: $15, 0.5 lb.

name: Timed Candle
description: Alchemist’s mixture burns at a precise rate for 12 hours. Marked in hours and minutes. Handy for timing spell durations – especially underground! $5, 1 lb.

name: Bandoleer
description: Carries 6 lbs. of throwing weapons (24 daggers, 12 packs of caltrops, 30 nageteppo, etc.). Wearer can reach them with Ready or Fast-Draw. $60, 1 lb.

name: Crossbow Rest
description: Lets a standing crossbowman brace while aiming. Takes a Ready to set up. $40, 2 lbs.

name: Crossbow Sight
description: +1 Acc for aimed shots. Iron, not fragile glass. $100, 1 lb.

name: Crossbow Sling
description: Totes a loaded crossbow “hands free,” a Ready maneuver away from shooting. Weapon safely re-slings itself when dropped (a free action). $200, 2 lbs.

name: Dwarven Whetstone
description: Gives edged weapons +1 damage for sharpness with first blow that connects after sharpening (1 minute/weapon). $500, 1 lb.

name: Bit and Brace
description: Useful for drilling peepholes. Does sw-2(2) pi++ per second to wood. $120, 5 lbs.

name: Caltrops
description: Take a Ready maneuver to deploy. Victims who miss a Vision-2 roll step on a number of spikes equal to margin of failure. Each inflicts thr-3 imp – based on his ST – to the foot. Caltrops that penetrate DR continue to do damage each turn until removed (two Ready maneuvers). Enough for one hex: $5, 0.5 lb.

name: Climbing Spikes
description: Strap-on spikes for both hands and feet allow scaling of vertical surfaces at no penalty. $400, 4 lbs.

name: Disguise Kit
description: +1 to Disguise skill. $800, 10 lbs.

name: Giant Spider Silk Cord
description: Supports 360 lbs. Per 10 yards: $100, 0.5 lb.

name: Grapnel
description: Throw to ST×2 yards. Supports 300 lbs. $80, 2 lbs.

name: Lockpicks
description: Basic equipment for Lockpicking skill. $50, 0.1 lb. Better kits are heavier because they include more tools. Good quality: +1 to skill; $250, 0.5 lb. Fine quality: +2 to skill; $1,000, 2 lbs.

name: Nageteppo, Flash
description: When hurled, everyone within 10 yards of where it lands must roll vs. HT or suffer Blindness (a Vision-Based affliction). Roll vs. HT to recover every turn. $40, 0.2 lb.

name: Nageteppo, Smoke
description: When hurled, fills a two-yard radius with smoke (-10 to Vision) for 5 seconds. $40, 0.2 lb.

name: Padlocks
description: For chests, strongboxes, etc. Cheap ones have DR 3, HP 4, and give +5 to Lockpicking; $20, 1 lb. Good ones have DR 6, HP 5, and give no Lockpicking modifier; $400, 2 lbs. Fine ones have DR 12, HP 5, and give -5 to Lockpicking; $8,000, 2 lbs.

name: Portable Ladder, 30’
description: Wooden slats attached to two hooked ropes. No Climbing roll required, once attached. Fits in a pack. $200, 10 lbs.

name: Portable Ram
description: Miniature, steel-capped ram with handles requires two to four users. Does sw+3d+1 cr every three seconds. Use highest ST plus 1/5 the total of all other ST scores. $150, 35 lbs.

name: Snorkel, 6’
description: Airtight bamboo tube with mouthpiece. $30, 1 lb.

name: Spy’s Horn
description: Carefully shaped hollow horn, open at both ends, allows a Hearing roll to listen through doors, shutters, etc., at a penalty equal to barrier’s (DR + HP)/5. $100, 2 lbs.

name: Traps
description:
Spring-loaded leg-hold traps. Roll vs. Traps to set. If chained or staked down, victim must break free from trap’s ST to move away.

Mini-trap: 1d-1 cr, ST 8; $80, 2.5 lbs.
Man trap: 1d+1 cr, ST 12; $180, 6 lbs.
Monster trap: 1d+3 cr, ST 16; $320, 11 lbs.

name: Backpack Alchemy Lab
description: Basic equipment for identifying potions and magic items with Alchemy skill; -2 to brew potions in the field. $1,000, 10 lbs.

name: Healer’s Kit
description: Basic equipment for one specialty of Esoteric Medicine skill. Also gives +1 to First Aid skill. $200, 10 lbs.

name: Holy Symbol
description: Ordinary religious symbol made of wood, cheap metal, etc., and blessed only by user’s personal faith. $50, 1 lb.

name: Holy Symbol, Blessed
description: Sanctified by a high priest. Gives +1 to rolls for Exorcism, True Faith, etc. (but not clerical spells). $250, 1 lb.

name: Holy Symbol, High
description: Sanctified by head of religious order. Gives +2 to rolls for Exorcism, True Faith, etc. $1,000, 1 lb.

name: Holy Water
description: Small bottle holds enough (1/2 pint) to damage an unholy creature with a suitable Weakness. Hurl it using the “grenade” rules; see Concoctions (p. 28). $15, 1 lb.

name: Manual
description: Allows default rolls for one “information” skill that normally has no default – Alchemy, Hidden Lore, etc. Roll at IQ-4 if Easy, IQ-5 if Average, IQ-6 if Hard, or IQ-7 if Very Hard. $100, 6 lbs.

name: Map
description: Rugged, foldable, and reliable map of explored dungeon, city, forest, etc. Unreliable maps are cheaper. $100+, 0.1 lb.

name: Tome
description: As manual, but also gives those who know the skill +1 to identify items, do research, etc. $500, 12 lbs.

name: Bull’s-Eye Lantern
description: Shuttered lantern with lens throws a 10-yard beam. Requires a hand. Burns for 6 hours on 1 pint of oil. $100, 2 lbs.

name: Burning Glass
description: Sets fires – but only in sunlight. $40, 0.25 lb.

name: Corrective Spectacles
description: Mitigator for Bad Sight. Large and heavy, like bottle-bottoms. Give DR 1 to eyes, but break if this is penetrated! $150, 0.5 lb.

name: Mirrors
description: Glass-covered bronze or lead. Hand mirror, useful for peering around corners: $15, 1 lb. Tall mirror, large enough to reflect Medusa’s gaze or fool stupid goblins: $125, 10 lbs.

name: Telescope
description: Gives Telescopic Vision 1 (2× magnification). $500, 6 lbs.

name: Tinted Goggles
description: “Alchemist’s goggles” grant Protected Vision, at the cost of -5 to Vision rolls. Give DR 1 to the eyes, but break if this is penetrated! $150, 0.5 lb.

name: Acid (Grenade)
description: Ordinary acid inflicts 1d-3 corrosion damage; DR protects normally. Can instead be used to burn through a mundane lock in 3d minutes. $10, 1 lb.

name: Alchemist’s Fire (Grenade)
description: Self-igniting sticky oil! A direct hit causes 1d burning damage/second for 30 seconds or until the target rolls on ground; armor DR protects at 1/5 normal. Tossed at the ground, it creates a two-yard-radius fire (1d-1 burn/second) for 30 seconds. $100, 1 lb.

name: Glow Vial (Utility)
description: Once separate pill is dropped into vial, glows brightly enough to eliminate darkness penalties in a two-yard radius for 12 hours. Includes cord for wearing around neck, light shows, etc. Liquid can instead be used to mark a glowing path through one typical dungeon level. $30, 0.5 lb.

name: Anti-Toxin (Drinkable)
description: Herbal antidote for one specific non-alchemical poison or venom. Completely halts effects of that toxin after 1d minutes. $20, 0.5 lb.

name: Garlic (Bundle)
description: Repels vampires. $5, 0.25 lb.

name: Wolfsbane (Bundle)
description: Repels lycanthropes. $5, 0.25 lb.

name: Bladeblack (Utility)
description: Deadliest manmade blade venom, from the legendary Assassins’ Guild. A living victim must make an immediate HT-5 roll or suffer 6d injury. $1,000, 0.5 lb.

name: Demon’s Brew (Grenade)
description: Respiratory agent made from demon ichor. Fumes affect a two-yard radius. Anything that breathes takes 2d injury, or only 1d with a HT roll. $500, 1 lb.

name: Monster Drool (Utility)
description: Generic blade venom made from giant centipedes, spiders, or whatever else is in season. Often used on whole quivers of arrows because it’s cheap. A living victim must make an immediate HT roll or suffer 2 points of injury. $20, 0.5 lb.

name: Oozing Doom (Grenade)
description: Contact agent made from slimes. Soaks clothing – or enters cracks in manmade or natural armor – in DR seconds. Living victims then take 2d injury, or only 1d with a HT roll. $100, 1 lb.

name: Agility Potion (Drinkable)
description: +1d DX for 1 hour. $700, 0.5 lb.

name: Alchemical Antidote (Drinkable)
description: Instantly negates all potions currently affecting the drinker. $400, 0.5 lb.

name: Balm of Regeneration (Drinkable)
description: Salve, not a potion. Heals user 2 HP at the cost of 1 FP, once per second, until he reaches either full HP or 0 FP. $900, 0.5 lb.

name: Death Potion (Grenade)
description: Fumes affect a two-yard radius. Targets that breathe take 4d injury, or only 2d with a HT roll. $1,000, 1 lb.

name: Fire Resistance Potion (Drinkable)
description: Immunity to fire damage for 1d hours. $500, 0.5 lb.

name: Flight Potion (Drinkable)
description: Flight at Move 10 for 1 hour. $3,000, 0.5 lb.

name: Great Healing Potion (Drinkable)
description: Heals 4d HP. $1,000, 0.5 lb.

name: Invisibility Potion (Drinkable)
description: Grants invisibility for 1d×10 minutes or until user attacks, casts a spell, etc. $2,250, 0.5 lb.

name: Invulnerability Potion (Drinkable)
description: +3 DR, cumulative with other DR, for 1d+1 hours. $2,100, 0.5 lb.

name: Liquid Ice (Grenade)
description: Target takes 2d burning damage on contact due to extreme cold – not fire. Armor DR protects at 1/5 normal. $250, 1 lb.

name: Magebane (Grenade)
description: Fumes affect a two-yard radius. Wizards who breathe them can’t cast spells for 1 hour. $1,400, 1 lb.

name: Magic Resistance Potion (Drinkable)
description: +5 Magic Resistance (and -5 to wizardly spells) for 1 hour. $1,600, 0.5 lb.

name: Major Healing Potion (Drinkable)
description: Heals 2d HP. $350, 0.5 lb.

name: Minor Healing Potion (Drinkable)
description: Heals 1d HP. $120, 0.5 lb.

name: Paut (Drinkable)
description: Restores 4 FP depleted for magic. $135, 0.5 lb.

name: Perception Potion (Drinkable)
description: +6 to Sense rolls for 3d×5 minutes. $700, 0.5 lb.

name: Sleep Potion (Grenade)
description: Fumes affect a two-yard radius. Living beings who breathe them must roll HT-4 or sleep for 16-HT hours. $500, 1 lb.

name: Speed Potion (Drinkable)
description: +1 Basic Speed and Move per dose (up to +3), for 3d×4 minutes. $550, 0.5 lb.

name: Strength Potion (Drinkable)
description: +1d ST (but no extra HP!) for 1 hour. $250, 0.5 lb.

name: Thieves’ Oil (Utility)
description: Rubbed on the body, gives +5 to all rolls to escape bonds, squeeze through openings, and break free for 1d hours. $700, 0.5 lb.

name: True Water (Utility)
description: Purifies up to 100 gallons of water in a manmade container. $750, 0.5 lb.

name: Universal Antidote (Drinkable)
description: Instantly cures all poisons affecting the drinker. $750, 0.5 lb.

name: Weakness Potion (Grenade)
description: Fumes affect a two-yard radius. Living beings who breathe them have -3 ST/dose (up to -12 ST) for 1d minutes. $800, 1 lb.

name: Wisdom Potion (Drinkable)
description: +1 IQ for 1 hour. $1,500, 0.5 lb.

name: Small Private Room
description: Located on the ground floor to the right of the common room, this chamber is available for parties who do not wish to drink with the hoi polloi. It costs $10 for the evening or $15 per day to rent, not including a tip for one of the serving wenches. The small area has a table seating six, several candlesticks, a couple of sideboards, and a window facing out toward the street.

name: Large Private Room
description: Identical to the small private room, but seating 12 and costing $15 an evening or $20 per day. It is also situated to the right of the common room, but its window faces out on the alley to the rear of the tavern.

name: Barfly’s Goblet
description: A 12-ounce cup that can alter the alcohol content of liquid poured in, for 1 FP per use. A beverage imbibed from the goblet counts as either half a drink or two drinks for Drinking and Intoxication (p. B439). Useful for getting others plastered or winning drinking contests! $5,000, 1 lb.

name: Dancing Broom
description: Keeping the most affluent taverns clean, this whiskbroom is enchanted to sweep the floor at Move 5. Adventurers who acquire one can have it sweep their tracks away, for -3 on others’ Tracking rolls! $8,500, 1 lb.

name: Knockout Gauntlets
description: These DR 4 gauntlets do no extra punching damage past the mundane +1, but if the victim has to make a knockdown (p. B420) or "kayo" (see Skull, p. 12) roll after being punched, he rolls at -2! $5,100, 2 lbs.

name: Lute of Racial Harmony
description: Causes all listeners to ignore the performer’s race while being played, including all reaction bonuses. Great for orcs, bad for nymphs! Costs 1 FP per use, regardless of performance time. Comes in other versions – the flute of racial harmony is equally common. $9,000, 5 lbs.

name: Returning Coin
description: A magical prank, of sorts, as the value gained rarely justifies the cost to make it. Activate the $80 gold coin.

name: Achewater
description: Grains steeped with rare twigs before distillation. “Good for what ails ya” – reduce all pain (p. B428) by one level for an hour, to a minimum of Moderate Pain. Moreover, if you weren’t in any pain before, you’re now in Moderate Pain! Pint: $6, 1 lb.

name: Crushroom Ale
description: From fermented spores. Anyone becoming drunk on crushroom ale automatically hallucinates. Roll 1d; on a 6, he has a genuine vision, as for Oracle (p. B72). Roll IQ in the morning to interpret it. Pint: $7, 1 lb.

name: Demon Rum
description: Made by real demons. Clerics generally disapprove – between swigs. Gives +1 to resist unholy (not wizardly!) curses, -1 to helpful cleric spells cast on the imbiber, for one hour. Half-pint: $10, 0.5 lb.

name: Orcish Bloodwine
description: It couldn’t really be made from elf blood, could it? Offering this horrid plonk in negotiations with goblinkin gives +1 to Diplomacy rolls. Bottle: $7, 2 lbs.

name: Polar Beer
description: Comes from the Frozen North. Never quite thaws. Gives DR 1 vs. fire for one hour, but costs 1 FP/15 minutes thanks to the shivering. Pint: $5, 1 lb.

name: Spider-Eye Spirits
description: What look like bubbles are actually hundreds of tiny eggs (not eyes). Roll Will-2 or Will-based Carousing to drink. Gives +1 to resist ingested poison for an hour; kills internal parasites in 1d minutes. Ounce: $8, 0.25 lb.

name: Vorpal Brew
description: A pungent, bubbling concoction that does 1 point of corrosive damage per shot! However, as any trace of alcohol nullifies this, patrons are safe unless this is their first drink of the night. Good for not-so-friendly pranks and showing off. Ounce: $10, 0.25 lb.

name: Whisker Gin
description: A merfolk secret recipe that (somehow) involves giant catfish whiskers. Doubles breath-holding time for one hour, after which the drinker loses 5 FP. Half-pint: $8, 0.5 lb.

name: Wight Wine
description: Supposedly made by wights, this pale amber beverage is actually made from grapes that grow on their barrows. Its pleasant taste belies its ability to sap a man’s courage; each glass gives a cumulative level of Fearfulness for 1d hours. There has been at least one scandal involving a tournament contestant “fixing” jousts by slipping wight wine to his opponents before the match. Pint: $3, 0.5 lb.

name: Coleopteran Mine
description: The translation of the notes from coleopteran (GURPS Dungeon Fantasy 3: The Next Level, p. 5) tongue to human is quite helpful. Apparently, one of the miners created this map when he hid his stolen valuables deep within. The mine should be abandoned by now, right? $200, 0.1 lb.

name: The Hamlet of Brisco
description: Directions to (and a decent map of) an abandoned goblin village far from the nearest road. The scroll is certain that the chapel contains something of tremendous value, but different handwriting warns that feral beasts now roam the streets. $100, 0.1 lb.

name: Lord Jauffre’s Undercroft
description: Supposedly, Lord Jauffre’s castle has a secret escape passageway, via a hidden connection between its undercroft and a natural system of tunnels. Any exit can also be an entrance, of course… $500, 0.1 lb.

name: Maned Rat Warren
description: A series of tunnels, supposedly occupied by “giant maned rats,” whatever those are (see below). More importantly, they horde gold and other shiny things, according to the notes. Surely a group of heroes can handle a few rats! $200, 0.1 lb.

name: Monkey Cove
description: That’s what’s written on the map, at least. It defines a thick patch of jungle-like vegetation some distance from the current location of the adventurers, with an extremely narrow river running through it. “Apes and treasure both abound,” says the author, with a distinct lack of specifics – other than a red circle. $100, 0.1 lb.

name: Tregonwell Sewers
description: To find a city larger than Tregonwell, you’d have to visit the capital itself, and this multi-page map purports to be the original excavation plans for its sewers! Anyone familiar with the city today can easily find underused branches that might house cults, criminals, or creatures (and treasure). $500, 0.25 lb.

name: Blowpipe Mount
description: A leather and metal necklace that holds a metsubushi in “ready” position; a ninja can then Ready and fire the metsubushi in one second. Only one blowpipe mount can be used at a time; swapping in a metsubushi for another takes two hands and five seconds, plus the time to ready the metsubushi. $10, 1 lb.

name: Climbing Pole, Collapsible, 10’
description: For climbing and poking. Breaks down to 2’ overall length; takes 10 seconds to assemble or collapse. Functions as a 10’ ladder or a 10’ pole. No Climbing roll required. Sturdy enough for climbing, but not for repeated combat use; if used as an improvised staff, it will no longer extend or retract. $100, 6 lbs.

name: Firebox, Ninja’s
description: A small insulated metal box containing a heated stone. It takes only one second to open, and two seconds to stow. It provides a ready source of heat for igniting torches or other flammables. The box is watertight, allowing it to be submerged and used after surfacing. Stays sufficiently hot to light fires for 24 hours; it can be reheated between adventures for no cost. $20, 1 lb.

name: Folding Raft
description: A cunningly built raft of straw, designed to fold down into a small pack. Comes with its own carrying bag, which also functions as part of the raft. Holds two SM 0 occupants sitting or one lying down, or 200 lbs., whichever is less. $150, 10 lbs.

name: Ninja-to Saya
description:
The sheath for a ninja-to. Rigid and hollow, it’s slightly longer than the ninja-to, leaving a space for concealing a small object; the sword itself retains its own Holdout modifier. The saya functions as a 2’ snorkel (great for hiding underwater!) and as a 3’ ladder (using the square ninja-to guard as a step).

It can be wielded as a baton (p. B273), or as a functional blowpipe (p. B275) to disperse poison or elixir powders (see Ninja Chemicals, p. 16). Finally, the ninja fastens it to his waist with a 6’ cord, allowing him to pull it up after him when using it as a ladder. Adds $300 and 1 lb. to a ninja-to’s cost and weight.

name: Tabi, Inflatable
description: Great for crossing watery obstacles without getting wet. These take 10 seconds each to put on and inflate, using the ninja’s own lung power and a small tube. Walking on water with these is slow (1 yard/second), and requires a roll against DX to avoid falling. Running on water is at Basic Move, but the roll is against DX-5! Otherwise, these provide DR 1 to the feet. $50 and 2 lbs.

name: Tabi, Inflatable, Acid-Resistant
description: As inflatable tabi, meant to allow the ninja to walk across corrosive surfaces. As above, except that these provide DR 3 against corrosion attacks such as acid and slime monster goo, but no additional DR against other attacks. $200, 2 lbs.

name: Tabi, Stealthy
description: These split-toed ninja slippers are especially soft and noise-reducing. Gives +1 to Stealth vs. Hearing rolls. $100, 0.5 lb.

name: Tabi, Traction
description: These split-toed ninja slippers give excellent traction, but are much less stealthy than normal tabi: -1 to Stealth vs. Hearing rolls, but +1 to Climbing (when the feet can be used) or to DX rolls to keep footing in slippery conditions or on narrow ledges, ropes, etc. $75, 0.5 lb.

name: Torch, Waterproof
description: A seemingly simple torch (see Dungeon Fantasy 1, p. 24) except that its chemically treated tar resists rain or splashes of water. If doused with sufficient water to extinguish a normal torch (GM’s call), it remains burning on 1-5 on 1d. Repeated exposures require repeated rolls. It cannot burn submerged, however – any immersion of one full second or more will extinguish it. $12, 1 lb.

name: Blinding Gas (Grenade)
description: Contact agent made from assorted natural irritant powders. Gas fills a two-yard radius. Any living creature with eyes must make an immediate HT-2 roll, or be blind for 1d minutes. If the victim can wash out all of his eyes (takes five seconds and an available water source), the blindness ends immediately. $300, 1 lb.

name: Mind Fog (Grenade)
description: Respiratory agent made from burned lacquer. Fumes affect a two-yard radius. Anything that breathes must make an immediate HT-3 roll. Failure means dizziness, confusion, and loss of focus: -3 DX and IQ for 1 minute. Success means only -1 DX and IQ for the same duration. Frequently used by ninja to disrupt pursuit or soften up a dangerous target. $300, 1 lb.

name: Paralytic Slime (Utility)
description: Blood agent derived from a mix of rare and deadly fungus and giant-insect venom. A living victim must make an immediate HT-2 roll or be paralyzed for 2d×10 minutes. Success means no effect. $500, 0.5 lb.

name: Firestarters
description: Variant alchemist’s matches with tiny internal strikers that the weakest psi can trigger via latent pyrokinesis. Anyone with Unusual Background (Psionic) can hold one and roll vs. Will + Psi Talent to start a fire in a second. Won’t ignite otherwise. Waterproof tin of 50. $30, 0.25 lb.

name: Hypno-Disc
description: Shiny metal disc – flat, like a big coin – etched with a complex pattern of shimmering, swirling colors. Ready in hand, gives +1 to Hypnotism skill. $250, 0.1 lb.

name: Psure-Test™
description: Put a drop of any bodily fluid on the little stick. If the subject is (more often “was,” for monsters) psionic, the thing wriggles like a worm. Waterproof tin of 10. $50, neg.

name: Squiddy Snacks
description: “Start your day right!” One meal of… uh, something with tentacles. While you maintain a steady diet of this – a month or more – you get +1 to the first roll for a Psionics ability you make each day (the first roll after your power item recharges). $5, 0.5 lb.

name: Telekinetic’s Webbing
description:
Belt and suspenders with loops for 20 lbs. of combat gear and gadgets. Has no effect on readying items by hand, but customizable ties and buckles let the psi match the layout of carried gear to his mental image of it, allowing him to pull things out quickly using Telekinesis.

Telekinetic uses of Fast-Draw are at +1 (cumulative with the +4 for Telekinetic Tether!), while items that require Ready maneuvers only ever take one maneuver – even if they would take longer to prepare by hand. Equipment can be returned to the webbing the same way. $160, 3 lbs.

name: Bloque (Grenade)
description:
Releases vapors that obstruct a specific ESP or Telepathy ability, Telekinesis, or a particular psionic attack. That ability cannot penetrate the fumes at all – if the line of sight from psi to target crosses the area, the attempt fails. Everything inside the area is immune (senses perceive an impenetrable cloud). Affects a two-yard radius for 1d minutes.

To price bloque, find the affected ability’s highest standard level on the Psionic Abilities Table (pp. 11-13) and multiply “Cost (Alt.)” by $10: $60 for Pyrokinetic Bolt bloque, $80 for Psight bloque, $150 for Battlesense bloque, etc. 1 lb.

name: Clarity (Drinkable)
description: +1 Will per dose (up to +3), for 1 hour. $750, 0.5 lb.

name: Expunge (Drinkable)
description: Imbibed willingly or forced upon someone suffering from a psi effect like Mind Control or Madness, instantly ends all noxious psionic influences. $200, 0.5 lb.

name: Pshield (Drinkable)
description: Grants Resistant to Psionics (+6) for 1 hour. $960, 0.5 lb.

name: Psibane (Grenade)
description: Fumes affect a two-yard radius. Psis who breathe them can’t use their abilities for 1 hour. $700, 1 lb.

name: Pslay (Utility)
description: This blade venom has no effect on most targets. A psi – anyone with Unusual Background (Psionic) – must make a HT roll at a penalty equal to Psi Talent. Failure means 2d injury. $50, 0.5 lb.

name: Pslay BR (Utility)
description: As pslay (above), but injury is 6d! $500, 0.5 lb.

name: Taurus Blue (Drinkable)
description: +1 Psi Talent per dose (up to +3), for 3d×4 minutes. This can boost Psi Talent past the usual six-level limit! $550, 0.5 lb.

name: Taurus Red (Drinkable)
description: Restores 4 FP depleted by psi. $135, 0.5 lb.

name: Fhtagn Wand
description: +1 with psi. Anyone with ST 5+ can brandish this twiggy little worm one-handed with the Knife skill. Used to strike, it does swing-1 crushing (Reach C, 1) or thrust crushing (Reach C); on defense, it parries at -1. $2,500, 0.5 lb.

name: Fhtagn Baton
description: +2 with psi. Anyone with ST 6+ can wield this slender tentacle one-handed with Shortsword or Smallsword. Used to strike, it does swing or thrust crushing (Reach 1). It can be used to fence with Smallsword. $5,000, 1 lb.

name: Fhtagn Rod
description: +3 with psi. Anyone with ST 10+ can wield this longer tentacle one-handed with Broadsword or Rapier. Used to strike, it does swing+1 or thrust+1 crushing (Reach 1). It can be used to fence with Rapier. $7,500, 3 lbs.

name: Fhtagn Staff
description: +4 with psi. Anyone with ST 7+ can wield this monstrous tentacle two-handed with Spear or Staff. Used to strike, it does swing+2 or thrust+2 crushing (Reach 1, 2). It gets +2 to Parry, like a quarterstaff, when used with Staff. $10,000, 4 lbs.

name: Arctic Clothing
description: Counts as winter clothing and gives +5 to HT rolls for cold (p. 30) in arctic climates. Also gives +1 DR vs. all damage, but -1 to DX if layered with armor. +1 CF and 5 times weight. Upgrade from free starting clothes: +$120, +8 lbs.

name: Camouflage Clothing
description: For one of arctic, desert, jungle/woodlands, mountain, plains, or swampland. Provides a bonus to Camouflage, and Stealth vs. Vision, in that terrain: +1 for +2 CF, or +2 for +7 CF. Weight is unaffected. Upgrade from free starting clothes: +$240 (+1) or +$840 (+2).

name: Elven Boots
description: Light boots (DR 1*) specifically designed to foil enemy trackers: -2 to Tracking attempts. In a group, only useful if everybody wears them. $50, 2 lbs.

name: Elven Cloak
description: A heavy cloak bought with the CF for camouflage clothing, matched to a particular terrain type. Gives the same bonuses as such clothing when worn, functions as an ordinary heavy cloak when wielded. A cloak with only this feature is $150 (+1) or $400 (+2), 5 lbs.

name: Hobnails
description: Added to footwear, these cancel the -2 to DX and -1 to active defenses – though not the movement penalties – for bad footing (p. 38), at the cost of -1 to Stealth vs. Hearing. $25, 1 lb.

name: Moccasins
description: Light footwear (DR 1*) optimized for sneaking around. Cancels -1 in Stealth penalties for encumbrance, crunchy leaves, etc. $40, 1 lb.

name: Swarm Suit
description: Reduces injury from stinging swarms by 1 HP, granting immunity to the mundane kind (p. 34). Light and tight; layering with armor (which keeps out swarms for only five seconds!) gives no DX penalty. Also protects against insect-borne disease (Fresh Air Is Good For You, p. 34). $80, 5 lbs.

name: Winter Clothing
description: Prevents -5 to HT rolls for cold (p. 30) in icy places such as arctic and high mountain terrain, and gives +1 DR vs. cutting damage. +0.5 CF and 2.5 times weight. Upgrade from free starting clothes: +$60, +3 lbs.

name: Bug Juice
description: Protects vs. insect-borne disease (Fresh Air Is Good for You, p. 34), but stinks: -1 to Stealth, +1 to enemy scent-based Tracking. Per daily dose: $2. 50 doses weigh 1 lb.

name: Dwarven Bagpipes
description: The loudest nonmagical noisemaker known! For signaling, see Noise (p. 28). Also designed to be as good as Sound spells for the specific purpose of starting rockslides (Go with the Flow, p. 35). $300, 8 lbs.

name: Elven Blind
description: Netting for concealing tents, parked wagons, etc. Total the Occupancy of every vehicle and the capacity of every shelter. Each blind covers four places’ worth of people, giving an extra +1 to the party’s Camouflage roll in any terrain; see Sites (p. 24). $160, 8 lbs.

name: Face Paint
description: Popular with scouts and ninja, this improves the bonus from camouflage clothing or an elven cloak (Garments, p. 16) by another +1 for two hours. No bonus by itself. Specify terrain type. Per use: $1. 50 uses weigh 1 lb.

name: Gnomish Army Knife
description: A mind-boggling spectacle of blades, flints, spoons, etc., for adventurers who begrudge the 1 lb. for personal basics (which it replaces). $100, neg.

name: Lantern Balloon
description: A little rice-paper balloon with a small candle inside. Sends a signal light skyward when lit (Smoke and Fire, p. 28). Single-use. $10, 0.75 lb.

name: Mapping Kit
description: Specialized tools and rulers give +1 to Cartography rolls to make maps. $50, 2 lbs.

name: Yurt
description: Portable felt shelter with collapsible wooden frame gives cover DR 1. Makes comfort (Sites, p. 24) “cost” one fewer benefit, so it counts as free to those with bedrolls, as one benefit for those without. For five: $480, 200 lbs. For 10: $1,200, 500 lbs.

name: Doom Cleats
description: A dwarven weapon of war, these wicked foot spikes also grant Terrain Adaptation (Ice). On arctic terrain defined as icy rather than snowy, let the wearer ignore all effects of bad footing (p. 38) and hike at full speed (not at ×0.50). Give +2 to kicking damage and +1 to Climbing, too, at the cost of -2 to Stealth vs. Hearing and +2 to enemy Tracking rolls. Permanently attached to DR 2+ foot armor (boots, sollerets, etc.). $400, 4 lbs.

name: Sandshoes
description: On desert or island/beach terrain defined as loose sand rather than hard, let the wearer hike at half speed (not at ×0.20). Can work as snowshoes at -2 to Hiking. Attach temporarily to footwear. $100, 5 lbs.

name: Skates
description: On arctic terrain defined as icy rather than snowy, let the wearer use Skating skill to move at ×1.25 speed on level ground (not at ×0.50). Give +1 to kicking damage, too. Attach temporarily to footwear. $60, 3 lbs.

name: Barding, Cloth
description: A full set of armor for skull, face, neck, torso, groin, and legs. DR 1. $275, 33 lbs.

name: Barding, Leather
description: As above, but DR 2. $688, 83 lbs.

name: Barding, Scale
description: As above, but DR 3. $1,760, 88 lbs.

name: Bridle and Bit
description: All that’s needed to lead the beast as a pack animal. Animal Handling is at -3 without it. $35, 3 lbs.

name: Lance
description: See p. B272. $60, 6 lbs.

name: Riding Gear
description: Reins, bit, saddle, blankets, and so on, as befits the specific creature. Without this much gear, all Riding rolls are at -3! $150, 15 lbs.

name: Spurs
description: Give +1 to Riding rolls for control, but not to stay mounted or avoid disaster. Noisy (-1 to Stealth vs. Hearing). $25, neg.

name: War Saddle
description: Heavy saddle with stirrups, high horns, and so on. Counts as riding gear and gives +3 to skill rolls to stay seated (and a 10 or less chance on 3d of staying in the saddle even if incapacitated). Includes attachment points for sheaths, quivers, etc. $250, 35 lbs.

name: Coin
description: Assume that any delver who isn’t completely illiterate (as barbarians often are) can count and evaluate coin: a copper farthing is $1; a silver penny, $4; and a gold piece, $80. Copper is $62.50/lb.; silver, $1,000/lb.; and gold, $20,000/lb. To avoid being ripped off, bring scales and weigh it all!

name: Anti-Magic Potion (Grenade)
description: Fumes casts Dispel Magic at skill 15 over a two-yard-radius. $720, 1 lb.

name: Bottled Sunlight (Grenade)
description: Fills a two-yard radius with sunlight, exactly as the Sunlight spell, for one minute. $400, 1 lb.

name: Demon-Bane (Grenade)
description: Fumes do 2d injury (DR doesn’t protect!) against all demons and anyone possessed by a demon in a two-yard radius. No affect on others. $1,000, 1 lb.

name: Alchemist’s Garb
description: Treated cloth apron, mask, and gloves prevent all ill effects from failures when rinsing off gunk, extracting venom, etc. Also screens out contact agents sprayed from the front. Can be worn as “armor” (DR 0) or with armor (bulky, -1 DX). $225, 5 lbs.

name: Cobweb Kite
description: Huge, spider-silk blanket – rigged to a backpack-style harness – unfurls after a fall of 40+ yards, guaranteeing a soft landing. $16,000, 8 lbs.

name: Float Coat
description: Complex belt-and-bladder arrangement gives +6 to Swimming to avoid drowning but -3 DX while inflated (1 minute to inflate or deflate). $100, 6 lbs.

name: Scroll Belt
description: Belt with 10 waxed leather cylinders for individual paper, cloth, or leather maps or scrolls. Waterproof, and prevents ignition by less than 10 HP of flame. Wearer can reach scrolls with Ready or Fast-Draw. Unrolling them takes another Ready. $60, 1 lb.

name: Shield Lamp
description: Tough (DR 6, HP 12) lantern clamps to any medium or large shield. Throws a five-yard beam, hands-free. Creatures subject to ill effects from light suffer these automatically if blocked! Burns 12 hours on 1 pint of oil. $200, 4 lbs.

name: Shield Lectern
description: Bolts to the back of any medium or large shield. Firmly holds a map, scroll, or open book where it can be consulted hands-free or written on with a free hand. $50, 2 lbs.

name: Dwarven Accurizer
description: Designed by dwarves to show elves how real archers shoot. Hefty headgear’s twin telescopes pivot into place (a Ready) to provide Telescopic Vision 1 (2× magnification). Gives +1 Acc! $1,200, 14 lbs.

name: Reflector
description: Concave reflector concentrates light where the wearer is looking. User flips it down over one eye and peers through a hole. Allows unpenalized reading, lockpicking, trap removal, etc., when darkness penalty is no worse than -3. $75, 1 lb.

name: Faerie Ink
description: Alchemical ink, sold by leprechauns, gives completely secret writing until exposed to special developer (the See Secrets spell will reveal it, too). Ink: $75, 0.5 lb. Developer: $75, 0.5 lb.

name: Portable Scribe
description: Copies ink writing on paper. Place page in press with sheet of paper, add alchemical fluid (vial good for 10 copies: $100, 0.5 lb.), and operate roller. Magic in scroll is transferred, leaving the old page blank. Takes 10 seconds/copy. $400, 15 lbs.

name: Scroll Case
description: Waterproof and fireproof bone-and-metal case protects 20 rolled paper, cloth, or leather maps or scrolls from the elements. Takes a Ready to open or close, 1d seconds to find a specific scroll. With shoulder strap: $75, 1 lb.

name: Wax Tablet
description: Erasable, reusable, waterproof writing surface. $10, 2 lbs.

name: Self-Righting Hourglass
description: One-hour model, graduated in minutes. Useful for timing potion durations. Weights and floats keep it upright in water jar. $160, 4 lbs.

name: Trap-Finder’s Kit
description: Gives a Traps bonus when actively searching for, disarming, or removing traps. Good kit (well-made probes): +1 to skill; $250, 2 lbs. Fine kit (mirror-on-a-stick, spring-loaded pincers, etc.): +2 to skill; $1,250, 10 lbs.

name: Universal Tool Kit
description: Gnomish modular tools will suffice for any non-esoteric skill that requires tools – Armoury, Engineer, Jeweler, Lockpicking, Smith, Surgery, etc. The last kit you’ll ever need! $12,000, 20 lbs.

name: Primer
description: Scholars may temporarily add 1 point in the subject matter. Anybody can study this for 15 weeks on the road or in town and then spend 1 point to learn its lore permanently. It has no other value to non-scholars. $25, 3 lbs.

name: Textbook
description: Scholars may temporarily acquire up to 2 points in the topic. A textbook can teach a skill permanently, just like a primer. Those who lack the skill can consult it in the field to get a default roll for a skill that normally doesn’t allow one: attribute-4 if Easy, attribute-5 if Average, attribute-6 if Hard, or attribute-7 if Very Hard. $50, 6 lbs.

name: Thesis
description: Scholars may temporarily acquire however many points the book is rated for – at least 3 points and sometimes much more for skills, usually 6 points for Languages. For everyone else, this is no better than a textbook. $25/point, 12 lbs.

name: Sketchy
description: Provides no points! Navigation is at -2. $25, 0.1 lb.

name: Cloth, Otherwordly
description: Per 100-square-foot bolt. Made from unusual materials that are either inherently magical or turned into fabric through a magical process: spun moonbeams, stabilized seafoam, felted tears, etc. The material has no immediate effect, but it can be very valuable in complex magical work; it gives +2 to Merchant skill if sold or traded to an enchanter or other dealer in magical items.

name: Cloth, Giant-Spider Silk
description: Per 100-square-foot bolt. A very durable fabric, suitable for armor use.

name: Cloth, Gauze
description: Per 100-square-foot bolt. This is extremely delicate cloth, much beloved of pixies (+1 to Merchant skill if selling them gauze) but generally suitable only for decorative use.

name: Cloth, Linen
description: Per 100-square-foot bolt. A pure, fine, white cloth, often used in priestly garments.

name: Cloth, Pashmina Wool
description: Per 100-square-foot bolt. This kind of wool is rather expensive but makes particularly pleasant, warm garments with a light weight.

name: Cloth, Plain Silk
description: Per 100-square-foot bolt. Has a fairly coarse weave, but using a fine fiber.

name: Cloth, Samite
description: Per 100-square-foot bolt. A finer, slightly shiny cloth made from silk fibers.

name: Cloth, Satin
description: Per 100-square-foot bolt. An extremely fine, smooth silk fabric.

name: Cloth, Velvet
description: Per 100-square-foot bolt.

name: Cloth, Wool
description: Per 100-square-foot bolt. Utility-grade woolen fabric, warm and sturdy but heavy.

name: Fur, Common
description:
Per 100-square-foot bundle. Pelts of common animals. If desired, roll 1d, 1d on this table to determine the specific animal.

Roll – Pelt
1-3, 1 – Seal
1-3, 2 – Monkey
1-3, 3 – Rabbit
1-3, 4 – Fox
1-3, 5 – Goat
1-3, 6 – Horse
4-6, 1 – Ox
4-6, 2 – Deer
4-6, 3 – Elk
4-6, 4 – Reindeer
4-6, 5 – Antelope
4-6, 6 – Ibex

name: Fur, Exotic
description: Per 100-square-foot bundle. Finer and usually small pelts from animals such as minks and foxes. If desired, roll 1d, 1d on this table to determine the specific animal.

name: Leather, Common
description: Per 100-square-foot bundle. If desired, roll on the table for common fur (above) to determine the animal.

name: Leather, Exotic
description: Per 100-square-foot bundle. Made from a monster or other unusual animal. If desired, roll on the table for exotic fur (above) to determine the animal.

name: Scale-Hide
description: Per 100-square-foot bundle. Leather made from fish or reptiles.

name: Leather, Contraband
description: Per 100-square-foot bundle. The leather is made from a hide likely to offend some intelligent creature. This is often the skin of a sapient being (human, elf, etc.); if desired, roll on the Race Table (p. 59). Necromancers aside, any member of the offended race reacts to the owner at -4.

name: Leather, Otherworldly
description: Per 100-square-foot bundle. Pelts from supernatural entities: angelic horses, astral tigers, demon skin, etc. Like otherworldly fabric, it has no immediate effect but is extremely valuable to the right people and gives +2 to Merchant skill if sold or traded to an enchanter or other dealer in magical items.

name: Fiber, Linen
description: Per pound. Roll 2d×3 to determine the weight of bales of fibers in pounds.

name: Fiber, Silk
description: Per pound. Roll 2d×3 to determine the weight of bales of fibers in pounds.

name: Fiber, Wild Silk
description: Per pound. Roll 2d×3 to determine the weight of bales of fibers in pounds.

name: Fiber, Wool
description: Per pound. Roll 2d×3 to determine the weight of bales of fibers in pounds.

name: Fiber, Pashmina Wool
description: Per pound. Roll 2d×3 to determine the weight of bales of fibers in pounds.

name: Fiber, Giant-Spider Silk
description: Per pound. Roll 2d×3 to determine the weight of bales of fibers in pounds.

name: Fiber, Otherworldly
description: Per pound. Roll 2d×3 to determine the weight of bales of fibers in pounds. Gives +2 to Merchant skill if sold or traded to an enchanter or other dealer in magical items.

name: Basin
description: A wide, open bowl (two gallons), appropriate for large quantities of soup, washing up, or draining the blood of sacrificial victims.

name: Bowl
description: A small ceramic bowl suitable for individual meals.

name: Cauldron
description: A blackened iron cooking pot with a capacity of about four gallons.

name: Drinking Set
description: A set of drinking paraphernalia for four, such as snifters and a decanter for brandy or a strainer and wide, shallow cups for unfiltered wine.

name: Fork, Cooking
description: A heavy fork, about a foot long, good for holding roasts during carving, or piercing and lifting large vegetables. If used as a weapon, does thr-1 imp; use Knife skill at -2.

name: Fork, Table
description: If used as a weapon, does thr-3 imp; use Knife skill at -2.

name: Goblet
description: A large (at least one-pint capacity), footed cup.

name: Knife, Table
description: A dull knife, not sharp enough for cutting damage or pointed enough for impaling.

name: Mortar and Pestle
description: Stone, about a pint capacity.

name: Pitcher
description: Ceramic, half-gallon.

name: Place Setting
description: A set of dishes and eating utensils. Roll 1d for the number of settings found.

name: Pot
description: A lightweight cooking pot, holding about two quarts.

name: Skillet
description: A 12-inch pan for cooking.

name: Spit, Cooking
description: A pointed metal bar large enough to cook a whole goat or sheep. Does not include posts to set it up on.

name: Tea Set
description: A pot for brewing and four small cups.

name: Banner
description: A flag large enough to cover a person or table.

name: Brazier
description: An open metal dish on a pedestal or short legs, for heating or cooking.

name: Censer/Incense Burner
description: A small, enclosed brazier used for incense, often on a chain so that it can be hung or carried around.

name: Clock, Complex
description: Like the simple clock (below), but with an elaborate display that may involve multiple hands, moving displays of celestial bodies, ringing bells, etc. The clock becomes very inaccurate quickly if moved while it is functioning.

name: Clock, Simple
description: An unremarkable timepiece driven by water or a pendulum. Keeps time for eight hours before it requires resetting the pendulum or refilling the tank. This clock doesn’t keep time well when it is moved.

name: Music Box
description: Plays a tune with small chimes when the crank is turned.

name: Painting, Encaustic
description: Pigments are mixed with hot wax for vibrant color and interesting texture.

name: Pennant
description: A colored strip of cloth, appropriate for tying to the end of a lance or spear.

name: Bench
description: Simple seating for two or three people, with no arms, back, or padding.

name: Chair
description: A solid wooden chair with a back and possibly arms.

name: Chair, Folding
description: A chair that collapses for transport, much like a modern director’s chair.

name: Couch
description: Well-padded seating for two or three, with arms and a back.

name: Footstool
description: Better versions are cushioned.

name: Headrest
description: Carved wooden headrest used by some societies instead of a pillow.

name: Mattress
description: A thick cloth sack filled with feathers. Since it is closer to a quilt than a modern rigid mattress, it can be rolled up for transport. Cost and weight are for a single-person bed.

name: Rug/Carpet
description: A piece of fabric heavy enough to stand up to foot traffic. Cost and weight are per square foot; roll 2d+2 for area in square feet.

name: Table
description: A small (two to three square feet) wooden table.

name: Table, Folding
description: Folds up like a director’s chair for easy transport.

name: Tapestry
description: A decorative wall hanging. Cost and weight are per square foot. Roll 3d+10 for area in square feet.

name: Tub
description: A portable, thin-sided metal tub, large enough for one person.

name: Comb
description: A comb for grooming, not a decorative comb left in the hair.

name: Cosmetics
description: Pigments, often in a fatty base. Cost is per ounce; roll 1d/2 for amount.

name: Grooming Kit
description: Brush, comb, razor or small scissors, and a few small pots of soaps, cosmetics, and/or perfumes.

name: Razor
description: Can be used in close combat with Knife skill, but cannot parry; does thr-2 cut.

name: Scissors
description: Small (2-3” blades) scissors for grooming or light cloth work.

name: Strigil
description: A dull, hooked blade for scraping dirt and oil off the skin.

name: Fan
description: Thin wooden slats or cloth or paper glued to a wooden skeleton.

name: Mask
description: A cloth domino or similarly shaped papier-mâché mask covering the area around the eyes. In Dungeon Fantasy worlds, it may be enough to protect the identity of masked avengers.

name: Parasol
description: Protection from the sun and rain for one person.

name: Parasol, Canopy
description: A large (three-yard diameter) parasol, typically carried by one person to shelter another.

name: Pipe
description: For smoking tobacco or medicinal herbs.

name: Seal
description: An elaborate pattern carved into a solid object to press on sealing wax.

name: Staff
description: A long stick for walking. It isn’t balanced for combat but could be used as a quarterstaff at -2.

name: Tinderbox
description: Fire-starting equipment, such as a flint and steel, and finely divided tinder to get small flames going.

name: Walking Stick
description: A short walking stick. If used in combat, treat as a cheap baton.

name: Wand
description: Used for pointing or as a status symbol. This version is not inherently magical.

name: Water Pipe
description: A large, freestanding pipe with two mouthpieces on the end of flexible tubes.

name: Wig, Large
description: An enormous hairpiece, extending well down the back or piled up several inches over the wearer’s head. Additional decorations (flowers, figurative displays, etc.) may be handled with embellishments.

name: Wig, Small
description: A hairpiece that simply covers the head, perhaps with a few decorative curls or braids.

name: Armillary Sphere
description: A model of a planet and its surrounding heavenly bodies, constructed as a series of concentric openwork spheres.

name: Astrolabe
description: A complex navigational instrument made from stacks of thin, inscribed plates indicating angles, paths of stars, and mathematical calculations. Gives +2 to Cartography and Navigation skills.

name: Globe
description: A world map on a sphere. It needn’t be a map of the world the delvers are on. The GM may wish to treat particularly high-quality and accurate globes as maps (Dungeon Fantasy 1: Adventurers, p. 26; and Dungeon Fantasy 4: Sages, p. 14) with a base weight of 2 lbs.

name: Orrery
description: A model of a solar system with planets rotating around a central body. It is geared like a clock so that the planets retain the proper spatial relationships to one another.

name: Quadrant
description: A quarter-circle-shaped navigational device. By sighting through a low-power spyglass along one side and consulting an attached plumb bob, the user can determine visual angles. Gives +1 to Cartography and Navigation skills (may not be combined with an astrolabe).

name: Loom
description: A portable backstrap loom rather than a rigid frame loom.

name: Sewing Needles
description: Four needles in a card or pincushion.

name: Dice
description: Common low-tech randomizers include dice with two sides, four sides, and six sides, though 20-sided dice existed as well.

name: Game Board and Pieces
description: Chess, checkers, backgammon, jackals-and-hounds, go, or another game with a playing board and pieces.

name: Game Tiles
description: Complex pieces for games that don’t require boards, such as dominoes and mah-jongg.

name: Playing Cards
description: Nonmagical (unless enhancements are added) but used for divination as well as gambling.

name: Monster
description: A toy dragon, demon, Elder Thing, or other extremely dangerous creature.

name: Mundane Animal
description: A dog, bird, fish, barnyard animal, or other beast one might see in everyday life.

name: Person
description: A baby, identifiable craftsman, priest, or warrior, or simply a generic humanoid doll.

name: Unusual Animal
description: A lion, giraffe, or other rare but mundane animal.

name: Amphora
description: A large (six-gallon or 2.75-cubic-foot) earthenware container with handles and a pointed bottom, excellent for planting in the ground. DR 1, 12 HP.

name: Basket
description: A wicker basket (one-cubic-foot capacity) with a lid and carrying handle, good for carrying treats to Grandma. DR 0, 4 HP.

name: Bottle/Jar
description: See Dungeon Fantasy 1, p. 24.

name: Bottle/Jar, Small
description: See Dungeon Fantasy 1, p. 24.

name: Box, Stone, Large
description: A box the size of a wooden chest but carved from soapstone. Attractive and durable, but extremely heavy. DR 4, 24 HP.

name: Box, Stone, Small
description: A soapstone box the size of a large book. DR 4, 7 HP.

name: Box, Wooden, Large
description: A wooden box size of a large book. DR 1, 5 HP.

name: Box, Wooden, Small
description: A box small enough to fit in the palm. DR 1, 2 HP.

name: Cabinet
description: An upright chest with a capacity of eight cubic feet (700 lbs.) and doors opening in front. DR 1, 12 HP.

name: Cabinet, Compartmentalized
description: As above, but with many small drawers or shelves. The one who packed the chest can find things in it in half the usual time.

name: Cabinet, Small
description: A smaller version of the cabinet, with a capacity of about five cubic feet (400 lbs.). DR 1, 9 HP.

name: Cabinet, Small, Compartmentalized
description: As above, but with drawers and shelves.

name: Cage, Large
description: A cage made from thin iron bars (DR 5, 6 HP each) spaced at one-inch intervals. The cage is about two cubic feet, big enough for a mid-sized dog. The cage has a latch, but no lock, so an intelligent creature can release itself.

name: Cage, Small
description: A smaller cage, about 200 cubic inches, suitable for birds, rats, and other small animals.

name: Cage, Small, Wooden
description: Similar to the small cage, but made of wood (bars have DR 1, 4 HP). Suitable for small birds and other animals that won’t try hard to escape.

name: Chest
description: See Dungeon Fantasy 1, p. 24.

name: Chest, Compartmentalized
description: As above, but divided into compartments and cubbyholes.

name: Chest, Small
description: A smaller chest, about two cubic feet or 100 lbs. capacity. DR 1, 10 HP.

name: Chest, Small, Compartmentalized
description: As above, but divided into compartments and cubbyholes.

name: Strongbox, Iron, Compartmentalized
description: As above, but divided into small compartments.

name: Vial, Iron
description: DR 3, 3 HP.

name: Block and Tackle
description: An arrangement of pulleys allowing users to lift very heavy loads. Using a block and tackle permits someone to lift up to BL×32 one foot per second. Multiple adventures and even draft animals can pull on the rope; total the BL of everyone involved.

name: Climbing Spikes, Improved
description: Instead of just having claws at the hands and feet, the improved spikes put additional claws around the knees and elbows for greater traction. In addition to granting +3 to Climbing skill, the claws allow the user to stay attached to a vertical climbing surface by the legs but freely use both hands (or, if necessary, hang on by the arms but use the legs freely). They also give +1 to damage with unarmed strikes.

name: Crossbow Grapnel
description: A crossbow with a special harpoon-shaped bolt and a spool of strong cord secured to a pulley at the end of the bolt. The extra weight of the line-bolt gives it range and damage as a crossbow with 2/3 the user’s ST (round up). However, it can fire the grapnel much farther than someone could throw it. The double thickness of cord supports 180 lbs., or a sturdier rope can be pulled through at a rate of ST feet per second. Additional spools are $50, 2.5 lbs.

name: Giant-Spider Silk Cord
description: Per 10 yards. See Dungeon Fantasy 1, p. 25.

name: Orichalcum Climbing Chain
description: A strong but lightweight chain with larger rings set every foot for grabbing. The chain cannot be broken, cut, or burned (though repeated heat-based attacks can make it too hot to hold on to). Cost and weight are per foot; roll 2d+4 for length.

name: Rope, 3/4”
description: Per 10 yards. See Dungeon Fantasy 1, p. 24.

name: Rope, 3/8”
description: Per 10 yards. See Dungeon Fantasy 1, p. 24.

name: Dragonhide Rope, 3/4”
description: Rope made from braided strips of treated dragon hide is resistant to fire (DR 10 against heat and flame attacks). Supports 1,100 lbs. Per 10 yards.

name: Dragonhide Rope, 3/8”
description: As above, but supports 300 lbs. Per 10 yards.

name: Elven Rope, 3/4”
description: Supports 2,200 lbs. Per 10 yards.

name: Elven Rope, 3/8”
description: Supports 600 lbs. Per 10 yards.

name: Lifting Sling
description: A comfortable leather seat capable of lifting or lowering an occupant up to SM +1. Includes ties so the user doesn’t fall out if killed or rendered unconscious.

name: Healer’s Kit
description: See Dungeon Fantasy 1, p. 26. Designed for one specific Esoteric Medicine specialty.

name: Prosthetic
description: A false limb or other body part. This is a mundane replacement like a peg leg or a hook hand, not a mystically powered cybernetic part, but it can partially replace the function of a lost limb. Roll 2d to determine the part.

name: Elven Limb Brace
description: If applied quickly after combat, this lightweight but sturdy exoskeleton gives +3 to the HT roll to determine the duration of crippling injuries. Roll 1d to determine the limb the brace is designed for.

name: Spider-Silk Bandages
description: Six patches of giant-spider silk, excellent for patching wounds. Gives +1 to First Aid skill; can be combined with bonuses from other medical gear.

name: Backboard
description: A broad board with shoulder straps and cords with which to tie equipment. It takes half as much time to locate and retrieve gear as from a backpack. Holds 70 lbs. of gear.

name: Carrying Yoke
description: A W-shaped frame that rests on the shoulder. A hand on the front balances the load in the back. It can be dropped as a free action, but it requires a hand to keep it steady while it is being used. Holds up to 100 lbs. of gear.

name: Potion Belt
description: See Dungeon Fantasy 1, p. 25. Roll.

name: Pouch/Purse
description: See Dungeon Fantasy 1, p. 23.

name: Bagpipe
description: An exceptionally loud instrument – so loud, in fact, that other bards within 10 yards have trouble hearing themselves and are at -2 to their own Bard-Song rolls.

name: Glass Harmonica
description:
A series of glass disks on an axle inside a box, spun with a crank, and played with a wet fingertip touched to the rims; the principle is the same as running a finger around the rim of a wineglass to produce a tone. The instrument’s supernatural tone quality gives +3 to any Bard-Song rolls, but it has a number of drawbacks.

First, it is not a particularly mobile instrument. It takes three seconds to set up on its stand or put away, and it must be stationary while it is played. Second, it is very fragile. The casing has DR 2, but any attack that does damage to it destroys the instrument. Third, because of its weird resonances, a critical failure while using it attracts the attention of Elder Things, who can be expected to appear before the end of the current adventure.

name: Harp/Zither
description: See Dungeon Fantasy 1, p. 24.

name: One-Handed Concertina
description: A tiny accordion that can be squeezed with the thumb and played with fingers on a small set of keys. Gives -1 to Bard-Song rolls, but it can be played with one hand. The other can be holding a weapon, hanging on to a rope, etc.

name: Wet Cloak
description: A long, hooded cloak with thin tubes of water running through it. Provides DR 3 against fire and burning damage for five seconds.

name: Pixie Stained-Glass Spectacles
